bib.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction", Leland McInnes, John Healy, James Melville. Preprint. The PDF is arXiv:1802.03426v3, stamped 18 Sep 2020 (title page: September 21, 2020). No venue is printed.

COVERAGE: 108,652 of 108,652 chars, all 63 pages including Appendices A-C and references. Nothing skipped. Figures were read by caption only, so curve values in Figures 8-11 are not reported. Pages below are printed page numbers, which match PDF pages.

CLAIMS
All numbers are from the paper's own runs, implementation and tuning. Quotes have ligature markers resolved and line-break hyphens rejoined, otherwise verbatim.

1. claim: UMAP had the lowest runtime on every dataset except the smallest.
   number: UMAP vs FIt-SNE / t-SNE / LargeVis, seconds: Pen Digits 9/48/17/20 (Eigenmaps and Isomap 2s); COIL20 12/75/22/82; COIL100 85/2681/810/3197; scRNA 28/131/258/377; Shuttle 94/108/714/615; MNIST 87/292/1450/1298; F-MNIST 65/278/934/1173; Flow 102/164/1135/1127; Google News 361/652/16906/5392.
   setup: Table 3, on a "Macbook Pro with a 3.1 GHz Intel Core i7 and 8GB of RAM". Subsampled or reduced: Flow 100000x17 (10%), Google News 200000x300, scRNA PCA to 1,000 dims. t-SNE = MulticoreTSNE, whose thread count for Table 3 is not stated. FIt-SNE uses multiple cores. LargeVis uses 8 threads. UMAP is single core ("these experiments were carried out on a single core version"). Single timings, no repeats or spread reported.
   quote: "MNIST 87s 292s 1450s 1298s 40709s –"; "UMAP consistently performs faster than any of the other algorithms aside from on the very small Pendigits dataset, where Laplacian Eigenmaps and Isomap have a small edge."
   where: p36, p38 (single core: p22)

2. claim: The speed gain over FIt-SNE is a constant-factor one and much smaller than over Barnes-Hut t-SNE.
   number: my ratios from Table 3: 1.15x on Shuttle up to 31.5x on COIL100; 3.4x on MNIST. Prose gives no number.
   setup: Figure 11, GoogleNews subsamples on a server with Intel Xeon E5-2697v4 and 512GB RAM. MulticoreTSNE and LargeVis single-threaded, with an 8-core t-SNE line also shown.
   quote: "Asymptotic scaling of UMAP is comparable to that of FIt-SNE (and LargeVis). On this dataset UMAP demonstrated somewhat faster absolute performance compared to FIt-SNE, and was dramatically faster than LargeVis."
   where: p42

3. claim: The full 3M-vector GoogleNews embedding took about 200 minutes, against days for MulticoreTSNE.
   number: ~200 minutes; "several days"
   setup: 3M x 300, cosine, the Xeon server. The t-SNE figure is not given as a measured time.
   quote: "was completed in around 200 minutes, as compared with several days required for MulticoreTSNE, even using multiple cores."
   where: p42

4. claim: Scale demonstration on integer data, with no comparison method.
   number: 30,000,000 samples, ~1.8M dims, ~2 weeks
   setup: sparse binary prime-divisibility vectors, "large memory SMP".
   quote: "an embedding of 30,000,000 data samples from an ambient space of approximately 1.8 million dimensions. This computation took approximately 2 weeks on a large memory SMP."
   where: p45

5. claim: kNN accuracy on the embedding matches t-SNE at small k and beats it at large k on some datasets. Fashion-MNIST is the exception at small to medium k.
   number: COIL-20 k=80 UMAP 0.899 vs t-SNE 0.789; k=160 0.803 vs 0.609. Shuttle k=3200 0.957 vs 0.828. MNIST k=3200 0.964 vs 0.946. F-MNIST k=100 0.790 vs 0.818; k=3200 0.730 vs 0.727. PenDigits k=160 0.951 (± 0.085) vs 0.949 (± 0.065), which overlap.
   setup: Tables 1-2. Stratified 10-fold CV for PenDigits and COIL-20, 10-fold for Shuttle, 20-fold for MNIST and F-MNIST. Also compared: LargeVis, Eigenmaps, PCA. Embedding dimension is not stated in Section 5.2.
   quote: "80 0.789 (± 0.118) 0.899 (± 0.058) 0.803 (± 0.100)"; "(but notably underperforms on the Fashion-MNIST dataset)"; "performs markedly better than t-SNE or LargeVis at non-local scales."
   where: p30-32

6. claim: The global structure claim is hedged, and the paper attributes much of it to initialisation.
   number: none
   setup: visual reading of Figure 4 (COIL20, MNIST, F-MNIST, GoogleNews), plus kNN at large k as a proxy.
   quote: "arguably preserves more of the global structure" (p1); "a significant contributor to UMAP's relative global structure preservation is derived from the Laplacian Eigenmaps initialization"; "The authors of that paper demonstrate that t-SNE, with similar initialization, can perform equivalently to UMAP in a particular measure of global structure preservation." (p49). The paper also credits the objective: cross-entropy "is also a significant contributor".
   where: p1, p30, p49

7. claim: Embeddings are more stable than t-SNE's under subsampling.
   number: 5% subsample; t-SNE n_iter raised from 1000 to 1500
   setup: Flow Cytometry, 1,000,000 x 17, normalized Procrustes distance between a subsample's embedding and the matching part of the full embedding. One dataset. Measures subsampling, not seed-to-seed variation.
   quote: "after sub-sampling on 5% of the million data points, the per point error for UMAP was already below any value achieved by t-SNE."
   where: p35-36

8. claim: Runtime stays nearly flat with embedding dimension and with ambient dimension, while t-SNE does not.
   number: scRNA tested up to the original dataset (20,921 x 26,774 per p25); embedding-dimension detail up to 6 (Figure 9b)
   setup: Figure 9 PenDigits, comparison to MulticoreTSNE because FIt-SNE cannot exceed 2 dims. Figure 10 Mouse scRNA PCA reductions vs original.
   quote: "t-SNE scales worse than exponentially while UMAP and LargeVis scale linearly with a slope so slight to be undetectable at this scale."
   where: p39-42

9. claim: Overall complexity is empirical, inherited from NN-Descent, with no theoretical bound.
   number: O(N^1.14) overall; O(kN) for optimisation
   setup: figure reported by the NN-Descent authors, not measured here.
   quote: "While no theoretical complexity bounds have been established for Nearest-Neighbor-Descent the authors of the original paper report an empirical complexity of O(N 1.14)."
   where: p21-22

10. claim: Hyperparameters: n trades fine against large-scale structure, min-dist is "essentially aesthetic", and low n on structureless data creates spurious structure.
    number: defaults a≈1.929, b≈0.7915; ϵ=0.001
    setup: Figure 1, uniform 3-D colour cube; Figures 2-3 PenDigits and MNIST.
    quote: "Low values will interpret the noise from random sampling as fine scale manifold structure, producing potentially spurious structure"; "results in a ≈ 1.929 and b ≈ 0.7915"
    where: p23, p57

LIMITS
The paper's Section 6 (p45-50) states these:
- No interpretable axes or loadings. Recommends PCA, NMF or pLSA when interpretability is critical.
- Noise: "UMAP can tend to find manifold structure within the noise of a dataset". It is worse with small samples and "Detecting when a spurious embedding has occurred is a topic of further research."
- Local over global: "if global structure is of primary interest then UMAP may not be the best choice". Suggests MDS or PHATE, which are costlier.
- Metric structure: "will not perform as well as some methods on quality measures based on metric structure preservation".
- Density is equalised: for a loose region and a dense region, "UMAP would attempt to put these local areas on an even footing."
- Small data: "small (less than 500 samples) dataset sizes" can give suboptimal embeddings.

Section 7 (p50-51) concedes that global structure is "hampered by the lack clear objective measures, or even definitions". It also calls an empirical study of the components still needed.

What the paper does not show:
- No evaluation of clustering (HDBSCAN or k-means) on embeddings.
- No evaluation or algorithm for mapping new points.
- No direct global distance-preservation metric among its own measures.
- No seed-to-seed quantification.
- No false-positive rate for noise.
- No repeated timings.

Dated: "t-SNE is the current state-of-the-art" (p2). The authors note the implementation has since been parallelised (p22), so the timings describe a single-core version.

BUILDS ON:
- Belkin and Niyogi, Laplacian eigenmaps (2002, 2003): theory and initialisation.
- Spivak, metric realization of fuzzy simplicial sets (2012).
- Barr (1986), fuzzy sets.
- Tang et al., LargeVis (2016): edge sampling and optimisation.
- Mikolov et al. (2013): negative sampling.
- Dong, Charikar and Li (2011): NN-Descent.
- van der Maaten and Hinton (2008); van der Maaten (2014).
- Lee and Verleysen (2011): similar effect to the truncated similarity.
- Critique cited: Kobak and Linderman, bioRxiv 2019.

CODE: pseudocode only, Algorithms 1-5, p18-21. Worth keeping, cleaned of extraction markers: "Binary search for σ such that ∑ exp(−(knn-dists_i−ρ)/σ) = log2(n)" (Algorithm 3, p19). Symmetrisation: "B = A + A⊤ − A◦A⊤" (p15). Check the exponent signs in Algorithm 4 against the page image, because the extraction shows D1/2.

FIGURES:
- Figure 1, p24, hyperparameter grid on the uniform colour cube. Shows spurious structure from low n at a glance, which fits the segmentation note's control.
- Figure 4, p29, algorithm comparison on four datasets. The evidence behind the global structure claim, and visibly qualitative.
- Figure 8, p37, Procrustes distance vs subsample size. The stability result.
- Figure 11, p43, runtime vs GoogleNews sample size. Shows comparable FIt-SNE asymptotics vs Barnes-Hut.
- Figure 7, p35, Procrustes alignment of UMAP vs t-SNE. Explains the metric visually.
- Figure 10, p41, ambient dimension scaling.

PROBLEMS:
- No embedded instructions.
- Extraction: ligature markers (/T_he, /f_i), damaged equations and small-caps, bold lost in Table 3.
- The paper itself has an unresolved citation at p22 ("[?, see]]belkin2002laplacian").
- Internal inconsistencies:
  - scRNA is 20,921 cells at p25 but 21086 rows in Table 3.
  - p28 says "angular distance in t-SNE which does support non-metric distances, in contrast to UMAP", which sits oddly with p22 saying NN-Descent works with "any valid dissimilarity measure".
  - The Section 5.4 list of timed datasets omits rows that Table 3 has (Pen Digits, scRNA, Flow).
  - "Pen digits" is described as 1797 8x8 images (p25), citing [1, 10].
- Prose vs table: "markedly better" at non-local scales is not uniform. PenDigits differences sit inside the ± bounds, and LargeVis exceeds UMAP at k=40 (0.959 vs 0.954).

COMPARISON WITH THE NOTES

MISMATCH
- data-science/01-classical-ml/notes/05-unsupervised-learning.md:162, "it can map new points", cited to the paper. The paper presents this only as future work: "allows for the potential development of techniques to add new unseen data points into an existing embedding" (p50-51), adding "Experimental versions of some of this work are already available in the referenced implementations." It gives no method or evaluation. The citation does not support the flat claim. If the library's `transform` is the basis, it needs its own source; I did not check the library docs.

UNDER-QUALIFIED
- Same line, "the faster alternative". True against Barnes-Hut t-SNE, but it carries no setup. The paper has UMAP only "somewhat faster" than FIt-SNE with comparable asymptotics, and slower than Eigenmaps and Isomap on the digits. The note's own digits dataset is the case with the smallest margin over t-SNE among those with a wide margin elsewhere: 9s vs 17s. The note's code uses scikit-learn TSNE, whereas the paper benchmarks MulticoreTSNE and FIt-SNE.
- Same line, "a claim to preserve more global structure". The word "claim" fits the paper's "arguably". What is missing is the concession at p49 that initialisation is a significant contributor and that t-SNE with similar initialization matched UMAP on one measure, plus the advice to look elsewhere if global structure is the main interest.

TENSIONS
- data-science/03-nlp/notes/07-llm-embeddings-as-features.md:324. The UMAP citation sits beside "Distances lose contrast in high dimensions" and the BERTopic pipeline. The paper supports general use and names clustering as a downstream task (p39), but never evaluates clustering on embeddings. The rationale belongs to BERTopic, not this paper. The same sentence group says HDBSCAN "finds clusters of varying density", while the paper says UMAP puts loose and dense regions "on an even footing" (p49), so density differences may not survive the reduction. The note does not mention this.
- 07:329, `min_dist=0.0`. Consistent with p23 ("Low values... will likely more faithfully represent the manifold structure"). No mismatch.
- 07:552, uncited: "Distances between far-apart clusters... do not carry meaning, and seeds move things around". The seed half is supported (p31: "necessarily different from run to run"). The distance half is not stated by the paper, which reads inter-cluster relations on MNIST as meaningful (p30). It is compatible with the local-over-global axiom at p45, but needs another source if it is to be cited.
- 07:631, density estimates unreliable at 384 dimensions: not from this paper.
- data-analytics/06-applied-analyses/notes/05-segmentation-and-rfm.md:351, heading "UMAP is for looking", and :382, "Keep UMAP for the picture". This comes from the lab, and it runs against the paper's stated position of "general purpose dimension reduction" for ML. Note 07 also uses UMAP as pre-processing. Worth attributing clearly, and the two notes differ in their advice.

VERIFIED
- Segmentation :361. The quote "can tend to find manifold structure within the noise of a dataset" is exact (p45), and the authors and preprint label are correct. Three additions are available:
  - The paper ties the risk to small noisy samples and says it decreases with more data.
  - The lab has 400 businesses (its README), under the paper's "less than 500 samples" caution at p49.
  - The lab uses n_neighbors=15 (lab.py:126), so it is not the low-n case from Figure 1.
- Segmentation :353, "a relative of t-SNE", is supported by Appendix C and p13.
- The year 2018 is the arXiv ID's year. The PDF read is v3 from 2020, and the runtime tables, FIt-SNE comparison and Kobak-Linderman concession all appear in this version. I did not compare v1.
